evals.prompt: hey can you write this up for the ops team? we need a one-pager they can open in a browser. Notes: Q3 incident count dropped 18% after the on-call rotation change; still waiting on legal for the customer-facing wording on the Feb outage; audience is managers not engineers. Don't make slides.
evals.expected_output: Builds the document immediately in one pass: scaffolds with `uv run python scripts/document/doc.py new`, writes the sections over the officekit:content marker, runs `uv run python scripts/document/doc.py toc` and `uv run python scripts/document/doc.py check`, writes a short NOTES.md, and hands back the file path and file:// URL. No subagent, no plan file, no approval gate, no server.
expectations: Treats the request as create-doc, not slides or video
Writes the document itself instead of delegating to a subagent
Does not create a BRIEF.md, a plan/PLAN.md, or a reports/ directory, and does not wait for plan approval before writing
Uses `uv run python scripts/document/doc.py` to scaffold and verify rather than hand-writing the HTML shell or hand-copying brand tokens
Produces exactly one file, projects/<slug>/<slug>.html, and does not start a preview server or a headless browser
Honors the audience note by pitching at managers, and reflects the unresolved legal wording rather than inventing it

evals.prompt: Add a short section to the ops memo about what we're changing next quarter: moving the paging threshold and adding a second reviewer for postmortems. Files are in evals/files/existing-doc/ (treat that as projects/ops-memo/).
evals.expected_output: Reads the existing one-file document and NOTES.md, inserts the new section in place, re-runs `uv run python scripts/document/doc.py toc` so the contents list picks it up, re-runs `uv run python scripts/document/doc.py check`, and appends the change to NOTES.md. Does not rebuild the document or re-scaffold it.
expectations: Reads the existing document and NOTES.md before editing
Edits the existing file in place instead of running `doc.py new` over it or starting a fresh project
Re-runs `uv run python scripts/document/doc.py toc` so the contents list matches the new section, then `uv run python scripts/document/doc.py check`
Keeps the section shape used by the document (a <section> with an id and an <h2>)
Does not hand-edit the region between the officekit:brand markers

evals.prompt: Turn the attached research notes into a Word doc I can email. If Word isn't possible just give me something I can print. Path: evals/files/existing-doc/
evals.expected_output: Stays on the single-file HTML track, says HTML is the supported deliverable and that it prints cleanly from the browser, and does not switch to a .docx, Quarto, or paged-PDF pipeline. Emails cleanly because the artifact is already one self-contained file.
expectations: Does not introduce Word, docx, Quarto, or Google Docs as the production engine
Tells the user standalone HTML is the supported document deliverable and that the browser's print dialog covers printing
Notes that the existing file is already self-contained and can be emailed as one attachment, rather than inventing a packaging or export step
Does not route to create-slides or create-video

evals.prompt: We're rebranding to teal. Update the brand and make sure the ops memo matches. Files in evals/files/existing-doc/ (treat as projects/ops-memo/).
evals.expected_output: Routes the identity change to init-brand / brand-agent, which updates brand/brand.json and regenerates derivatives. Then propagates it into the document with `uv run python scripts/document/doc.py refresh`, because a standalone document embeds a copy of the token sheet. Does not hand-edit colors in the document.
expectations: Routes the brand change to init-brand rather than editing the document's CSS or the generated token sheet
Does not hand-edit values inside the officekit:brand region of the document
Propagates the change with `uv run python scripts/document/doc.py refresh` after the brand is regenerated
Recognizes that the document carries an embedded brand copy that goes stale, and that `doc.py check` detects it
